title: Iliad, Book I — Proem & Opening Quarrel
author: Homer
source_notes: Greek text from Monro & Allen (Oxford); English translation by Samuel Butler, 1898.
reading_notes: The proem (lines 1-7) names the wrath of Achilles as the theme. Then Homer turns to the narrative proper: a priest of Apollo, Chryses, comes to the Achaean camp to ransom his captured daughter Chryseis. Agamemnon refuses insultingly. Chryses prays to Apollo, who sends a plague.

lines.english: Sing, O goddess, the anger of Achilles son of Peleus,
lines.gloss: μῆνιν = 'wrath, anger' (accusative, object of ἄειδε); ἄειδε = 'sing!' (imperative); θεά = 'goddess' (vocative, the Muse); Πηληϊάδεω = 'of the son of Peleus' (genitive); Ἀχιλῆος = 'of Achilles' (genitive).

lines.original: οὐλομένην, ἣ μυρί᾽ Ἀχαιοῖς ἄλγε᾽ ἔθηκε,
lines.english: that brought countless ills upon the Achaeans.
lines.gloss: οὐλομένην = 'destructive, accursed' (accusative, modifies μῆνιν); ἣ = 'which' (nominative feminine); μυρί᾽ = 'countless' (accusative plural); Ἀχαιοῖς = 'upon the Achaeans' (dative plural); ἄλγε᾽ = 'sorrows' (accusative plural); ἔθηκε = 'placed' (aorist of τίθημι).

lines.original: πολλὰς δ᾽ ἰφθίμους ψυχὰς Ἄϊδι προΐαψεν
lines.english: Many a brave soul did it send hurrying down to Hades,
lines.gloss: πολλὰς = 'many' (accusative plural feminine); δ᾽ = 'and'; ἰφθίμους = 'mighty, valiant'; ψυχὰς = 'souls' (accusative plural); Ἄϊδι = 'to Hades' (dative); προΐαψεν = 'sent forth, hurled' (aorist).

lines.original: ἡρώων, αὐτοὺς δὲ ἑλώρια τεῦχε κύνεσσιν
lines.english: and many a hero did it yield a prey to dogs
lines.gloss: ἡρώων = 'of heroes' (genitive plural); αὐτοὺς = 'them' (accusative); δὲ = 'and'; ἑλώρια = 'spoils, prey' (accusative plural); τεῦχε = 'made' (imperfect of τεύχω); κύνεσσιν = 'to dogs' (dative plural).

lines.original: οἰωνοῖσί τε πᾶσι, Διὸς δ᾽ ἐτελείετο βουλή,
lines.english: and vultures, for so were the counsels of Jove fulfilled
lines.gloss: οἰωνοῖσί = 'to birds of prey' (dative plural); τε = 'and'; πᾶσι = 'all' (dative plural); Διὸς = 'of Zeus' (genitive); δ᾽ = 'and'; ἐτελείετο = 'was being accomplished' (imperfect passive of τελείω); βουλή = 'plan, will' (nominative).

lines.original: ἐξ οὗ δὴ τὰ πρῶτα διαστήτην ἐρίσαντε
lines.english: from the day on which the son of Atreus, king of men,
lines.gloss: ἐξ οὗ = 'from which (time)' (relative); δὴ = 'indeed'; τὰ πρῶτα = 'at first' (adverbial); διαστήτην = 'stood apart' (aorist dual of διΐστημι); ἐρίσαντε = 'having quarreled' (aorist participle, dual).

lines.original: Ἀτρεΐδης τε ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν καὶ δῖος Ἀχιλλεύς.
lines.english: and great Achilles, first fell out with one another.
lines.gloss: Ἀτρεΐδης = 'son of Atreus' (Agamemnon, nominative); τε ... καὶ = 'both ... and'; ἄναξ = 'lord' (nominative); ἀνδρῶν = 'of men' (genitive plural); δῖος = 'divine' (nominative); Ἀχιλλεύς = 'Achilles'.

lines.original: τίς τ᾽ ἄρ σφωε θεῶν ἔριδι ξυνέηκε μάχεσθαι;
lines.english: And which of the gods set them to contend in such strife?
lines.gloss: τίς = 'who?' (nominative); τ᾽ ἄρ = 'then' (particles); σφωε = 'them two' (accusative dual); θεῶν = 'of the gods' (genitive plural); ἔριδι = 'in strife' (dative); ξυνέηκε = 'set together, provoked' (aorist of συνίημι); μάχεσθαι = 'to fight' (infinitive).

lines.original: Λητοῦς καὶ Διὸς υἱός· ὁ γὰρ βασιλῆϊ χολωθεὶς
lines.english: The son of Leto and Zeus; for he, angry with the king,
lines.gloss: Λητοῦς = 'of Leto' (genitive); καὶ = 'and'; Διὸς = 'of Zeus' (genitive); υἱός = 'son' (nominative, i.e., Apollo); ὁ = 'he'; γὰρ = 'for'; βασιλῆϊ = 'at the king' (dative); χολωθεὶς = 'having been angered' (aorist passive participle).

lines.original: νοῦσον ἀνὰ στρατὸν ὄρσε κακήν, ὀλέκοντο δὲ λαοί,
lines.english: sent a foul plague through the host, and the people began to die,
lines.gloss: νοῦσον = 'plague, disease' (accusative); ἀνὰ = 'up through' (prep. + accusative); στρατὸν = 'army' (accusative); ὄρσε = 'stirred up' (aorist of ὄρνυμι); κακήν = 'evil, foul' (accusative feminine); ὀλέκοντο = 'were perishing' (imperfect middle); λαοί = 'peoples' (nominative plural).

lines.english: because the son of Atreus had dishonored Chryses his priest,
lines.gloss: οὕνεκα = 'because'; τὸν Χρύσην = 'Chryses' (accusative); ἠτίμασεν = 'dishonored' (aorist of ἀτιμάζω); ἀρητῆρα = 'priest' (accusative).

lines.original: Ἀτρεΐδης· ὁ γὰρ ἦλθε θοὰς ἐπὶ νῆας Ἀχαιῶν
lines.english: son of Atreus. For he had come to the Achaeans' swift ships
lines.gloss: Ἀτρεΐδης = '(the) son of Atreus' (nominative); ὁ = 'he' (Chryses); γὰρ = 'for'; ἦλθε = 'came' (aorist of ἔρχομαι); θοὰς = 'swift' (accusative plural); ἐπὶ = 'to' (prep. + accusative); νῆας = 'ships' (accusative plural); Ἀχαιῶν = 'of the Achaeans' (genitive plural).

lines.original: λυσόμενός τε θύγατρα φέρων τ᾽ ἀπερείσι᾽ ἄποινα,
lines.english: to ransom his daughter, bringing boundless ransom,
lines.gloss: λυσόμενός = 'to ransom' (future middle participle); τε = 'and'; θύγατρα = 'daughter' (accusative); φέρων = 'bringing' (nominative participle); ἀπερείσι᾽ = 'boundless, unmeasured' (accusative plural); ἄποινα = 'ransom' (accusative plural neuter).

lines.original: στέμμα τ᾽ ἔχων ἐν χερσὶν ἑκηβόλου Ἀπόλλωνος
lines.english: holding in his hand the wreath of Apollo the far-darter
lines.gloss: στέμμα = 'wreath, fillet' (accusative); τ᾽ = 'and'; ἔχων = 'holding' (nominative participle); ἐν χερσὶν = 'in his hands' (dative plural of χείρ); ἑκηβόλου = 'far-shooting' (genitive, epithet of Apollo); Ἀπόλλωνος = 'of Apollo' (genitive).
